themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 10 reports THIS WEEK, up 789% from the 1.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting either a disease outbreak, environmental contamination, or pest population crisis in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.43)
789% spike in dead animal reports in the past 7 days
Magnitude suggests cluster rather than random distribution
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene about possible disease clusters or contamination triggering deaths
Investigate whether residents have observed pattern (location, type of animals, timing) suggesting environmental cause or pest control incident

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints jumped to 4 reports THIS WEEK (up 433% from 0.8 weekly average) and abandoned bike complaints also spiked to 4 THIS WEEK (up 433%), suggesting either recent storm damage, construction activity, or organized dumping affecting street infrastructure.
evidence: Street sign damage: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score: 4.91)
Abandoned bikes: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score: 4.91)
Simultaneous spike in two street-level complaint categories suggests common cause
reporting_angles: Determine whether recent weather event (high winds, storm) caused the sign damage and debris
Investigate if bike share rebalancing or bike theft pattern is driving abandoned bike spike

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints reached 3 reports last week, a 2300% spike from the 0.1 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69), indicating a potential widespread tree disease, pest infestation, or environmental stressor in the district.
evidence: Dead/dying tree complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Highest z-score spike in entire dataset, indicating statistically extreme anomaly
Damaged tree complaints also chronically elevated (310 over 90 days), suggesting ongoing tree health issues
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks Department about disease or pest survey results in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens; ask about emerald ash borer, Asian longhorned beetle, or other active threats
Interview arborists or community gardeners about visible signs of tree stress; map where dead trees are concentrated (parks vs. street trees)

themes_detail.label: Rodent & Dumping Convergence
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked 174% to 12 reports 2 weeks ago (7.69 z-score), and illegal dumping complaints jumped 186% to 25 reports during the same period (5.15 z-score), suggesting unsanitary conditions and vector habitat across the neighborhood.
evidence: Rodent complaints: 12 two weeks ago vs. 4.4 weekly average (174% increase, z-score: 7.69)
Illegal dumping complaints: 25 two weeks ago vs. 8.8 weekly average (186% increase, z-score: 5.15)
Concurrent spike in two related vectors suggests shared root cause (sanitation, waste management failure, or specific contaminated site)
reporting_angles: Map illegal dumping reports to identify hot spots; investigate whether specific blocks lack adequate sanitation or have broken waste infrastructure
Interview NYC Health Department about rodent control efforts and whether dumping sites are creating vector breeding grounds; request inspection data

themes_detail.label: Bike Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Bike rack complaints surged to 4 reports last week, a 700% spike from the 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.0), occurring alongside the 433% spike in abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK, suggesting systemic bike parking and safety infrastructure failure.
evidence: Bike rack complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 7.0)
Abandoned bike complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score: 4.91)
Back-to-back spikes in bike infrastructure complaints suggest cumulative failure or new policy/construction impact
reporting_angles: Determine whether DOT bike rack installations or repairs are stalled; check if Citi Bike rebalancing operations have changed
Interview local cyclists about whether bike theft or lack of secure parking is driving abandoned bikes
